title: Branch-mode fleet sync: agents, branches, locks
goal: Keep branch-mode fleets in sync: publish my agents' lifecycle, state, branch status and file-lock traffic as session events, and maintain a live, validated view of everyone else's agents, branches, locks and conflicts.
scope_in: Publishers: `agent.spawn` (clear `agent_id, owner, mode:'command_post'|'branch'`; encrypted `label?, branch?, worktree?, model?`), `agent.state` (clear `agent_id, state, since`; state MUST be a CT-STATE-MAP key; <= 2 frames per agent per second, identical consecutive states not re-sent), `agent.exit` (`outcome:'ok'|'error'|'canceled'`, `error_code?`, encrypted `detail?`), `branch.update` (encrypted `agent_id, branch, head, ahead, behind, dirty`).

File locks: send `file.lock` `acquire|release` with `path_hmac` (from C056 `pathHmac`) and encrypted `path`; handle server-originated `deny|expire`; bridge to the local lock client from lane C018 through an injected `LockBackend` so local and remote locks share one API.
`conflict.detected {agent_ids, path_hmacs}` receiver (encrypted `paths?` shown when decryptable) and a sender for locally detected conflicts.
Fleet model: per-member agents map, states, branch status, lock table keyed by `path_hmac` with TTL (`ttl_ms`), conflict list; rebuilt deterministically from replayed frames.
Bridge from the local agent bus (lane C025 events from lanes C014/C017) to publishers, rate-limited and coalesced; unknown incoming states rendered as a generic working state.
scope_out: Worktree creation (C017), local lock semantics (C018), state machine (C014), fleet panel UI (C042) and conflict UX (C078).
Session wiring, decode and crypto: lanes C057, C056.
Command-post queue claim semantics: lane C058/C075.
build_against: the mock backend (lane C007): REST from OpenAPI plus the WebSocket relay simulator, started in-process with `startMockBackend()` from @centcom/testkit; no real backend is needed. The relay simulator arbitrates locks on `path_hmac` (acquire/deny/release/expire by ttl) and enforces `max_parallel_agents` checks on `agent.spawn`. Fixtures: contracts/fixtures/events/agent.*.json, branch.update.json, file.lock.json, conflict.detected.json and contracts/state-map.json. Three in-process clients model the G5 scenario.
interfaces: `new FleetSync(session: SessionHandle, o: { bus: EventBus; locks: LockBackend; ring: () => KeyRing; clock })`; `start(): void`, `stop(): void`

Publishers: `spawn(a: { agentId; mode: 'command_post'|'branch'; label?; branch?; worktree?; model? })`, `setState(agentId: string, state: StateName)`, `exit(agentId, outcome, errorCode?, detail?)`, `updateBranch(b: { agentId; branch; head; ahead; behind; dirty })`, `reportConflict(agentIds: string[], paths: string[])`
Locks: `acquire(agentId, path, ttlMs?): Promise<'granted'|'denied'>`, `release(agentId, path)`; `interface LockBackend { acquire(...); release(...) }`
Model: `fleet(): FleetView = { members: { memberId: string; agents: AgentView[] }[]; locks: LockView[]; conflicts: ConflictView[] }`; events `changed`, `conflict`, `lock-denied`
acceptance: `setState` with a name not in contracts/state-map.json throws `UnknownStateError` locally (nothing sent); all 60 names in the map are accepted; identical consecutive states send 1 frame, and 10 changes in 1 s for one agent send <= 2 frames.

`agent.state` and `agent.exit` frames have cleartext-only or hybrid shape exactly per the catalogue: `agent.state` has no `ct`; `agent.spawn` `ct` decrypts to label/branch/worktree/model and the cleartext part contains none of those.

`acquire(agt, 'src/a.ts')` sends `file.lock` with `action:'acquire'`, a `path_hmac` equal to C056's `pathHmac(ring, kid, 'src/a.ts')`, and a `ct` holding the path; the same path from two agents: first gets `granted`, second gets `denied` from the server's `deny` and `lock-denied` fires.
A lock with `ttl_ms: 30000` that the holder neither releases nor refreshes shows as expired in `fleet().locks` after the server `expire` frame, and the local `LockBackend` is told to release.
`branch.update` is sent encrypted-only; no `branch` string appears in cleartext anywhere on the wire (simulator capture scan).
Rebuilding the view by replaying frames 1..N from fixtures twice yields identical `fleet()` (deterministic, idempotent for duplicates).
Receiving an `agent.state` with a state name unknown to the local map shows the generic working state and a debug log, and the view is still updated.
A `conflict.detected` frame with `agent_ids` that include one of mine fires `conflict` once with both ids and decrypted paths when readable (else only hmacs).
`spawn` beyond `max_parallel_agents` (from the entitlement/limits in `welcome`) surfaces the relay's rejection as a typed error and the local agent is not started by this lane.
tests: fleet/publisher.test.ts: state-name validation across all state-map keys, rate limit, hybrid/clear shapes.
fleet/locks.test.ts: acquire/deny/release/expire against the simulator, hmac consistency across two clients and sessions (different sessions give different hmacs).
fleet/model.test.ts: replay determinism, unknown state, duplicate frames.
fleet/three-clients.test.ts: G5-style scenario with three SessionClients, locks and a conflict.
fleet/privacy.test.ts: scans captured frames for branch/path/worktree/model strings in cleartext.
guardrails: MUST send paths, branch names, worktree paths and model names only inside `ct`; the only path-derived cleartext is `path_hmac` computed by C056.

MUST validate every outgoing `agent.state.state` against contracts/state-map.json keys; MUST NOT invent states. Client-local states (offline, reconnecting, quota-reached, teammate-*) MUST NOT be sent as agent states.
MUST respect <= 2 `agent.state` frames/agent/s and not re-send identical consecutive states.
Locks are advisory: MUST NOT block a local edit solely on a remote lock when offline; MUST treat server `deny` as authoritative and never retry-spin (back off to the caller).
MUST NOT trust `owner`/`from` claims over the roster; ignore agent events from non-members.
failure_modes: Disconnected while holding locks -> locks are considered unconfirmed; on reconnect re-send `acquire` for held paths and accept `deny` by releasing locally with a conflict event.
Lock table drift after a gap -> rebuilt from replay/snapshot; `fleet()` is a pure reducer so no manual repair.
notes: `reaction` and `comment.add` kinds are out of this lane (lane C080). The ttl refresh cadence for long-held locks is a client policy (refresh at ttl/2) since the contract fixes only `ttl_ms`.
